name: South Korea
tagline: The academic year starts in March, and that decides everything else
summary: Korea keeps a separate admissions track for applicants who did all twelve years of school abroad, and an IB Diploma fits it: no Suneung, a small international pool, and a decision on transcript, essays and often an interview. The catch is the calendar. The Korean year begins in March, and March 2027 is out of reach for a May 2027 candidate, so the real choices are September 2027 on predicted grades or March 2028 with results. English-taught degrees are concentrated at Yonsei's Underwood International College, KAIST, POSTECH, UNIST and GIST, plus specific divisions elsewhere.
whyConsider: Underwood International College is a genuine full-English liberal-arts college inside Yonsei, a major research university — sixteen majors, about 3,000 students from more than seventy countries — and it admits for both the March and the September intake.

The international track is document-and-interview based and separate from the domestic Suneung competition, which suits a student who writes well and which makes universities reachable that are not reachable domestically.

KAIST teaches essentially its whole undergraduate programme in English, and exempts scholarship holders from tuition for eight semesters with a monthly allowance on top, decided from the admission application itself.
KAIST publishes tuition of 3,433,000 KRW a semester, which is modest for an English-taught degree.
Seoul is affordable compared with Tokyo, Singapore or Hong Kong once you are out of the central districts, and university dormitories are cheap and usually allocated with the offer.
watchOuts: March 2027 is not available to a May 2027 IB candidate, and a page that says 'Autumn 2027' while listing March deadlines is describing two different years. September 2027 or March 2028 are the choices.

Every September 2027 decision is made before 6 July. KAIST's regular round closes 14 January 2027 and decides 25 March; Yonsei UIC's second round runs in March 2027 and decides in June. Predicted grades carry the application.

No May 2027 IB candidate can use the 2027 Global Korea Scholarship on either track: it needs a graduation certificate by 31 December 2026. Plan for 2028, when the Embassy Track depends on your nationality and the University Track's UIC Program — science and engineering at thirteen named universities, none of them the ones above — is open to every nationality.

There is no central portal and no shared calendar. Several universities run their applications on Uwayapply, a separate national platform, and several publish each round only four to six months ahead.

Yonsei UIC now requires proof of English from every applicant from the 2027 intake. IB DP English A (Language and Literature, or Literature) counts with no minimum score, and so does a Medium of Instruction certificate from a school that teaches entirely in English; English B is not listed.
The only official Korean tuition figure quoted here is KAIST's, and its page states no price year. Ask each other university for its costs.

ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: There is no national rule. Each university reads the IB transcript inside its own international admission track, and the category that matters is the one for applicants who completed the entire curriculum outside Korea — Seoul National University calls it 글로벌인재특별전형 II, 'those who completed the entire curriculum overseas'. That category is what removes the Suneung from the question. None of the university pages linked from this page publishes a minimum IB point score, and anything quoted on an agent site should be treated as unverified.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: No national conversion table. The Global Korea Scholarship publishes its own CGPA thresholds — 80 per cent on a 100-point scale, or the top 20 per cent of the class, or a CGPA at or above 2.64/4.0, 2.80/4.3, 2.91/4.5 or 3.23/5.0 — but how an IB transcript is read against them is not stated and is the question to put to NIIED before applying.
notes: The route an IB student from a Danish gymnasium uses is the twelve-years-abroad category, not the general foreigner category, and the two have different documentary requirements at several universities.

Some universities accept the IB as proof of English and others insist on IELTS or TOEFL. Yonsei UIC lists IB DP English A among its accepted proofs for 2027, with no minimum score; check every other university separately.
TOPIK is normally required only for Korean-taught programmes, but a few English-taught degrees ask for a level by graduation. Check the small print rather than the marketing page.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Concentrated rather than widespread, and named rather than general. Yonsei UIC (sixteen majors), KAIST, POSTECH (for international undergraduates since Fall 2026), UNIST and GIST teach undergraduates in English; Korea University's Division of International Studies, Sungkyunkwan's Global tracks, Ewha's Division of International Studies and Kyung Hee's College of International Studies are the English-medium entry points at otherwise Korean-medium universities. No national total is given here.
language.englishProof: Set per university. Yonsei UIC requires proof of English from every applicant from the 2027 intake, and accepts an IB DP English A (Language and Literature, or Literature) result with no minimum score, a TOEFL, IELTS or CEFR certificate, or a Medium of Instruction certificate for a school curriculum taught entirely in English. UNIST asks for an English test report. Elsewhere, ask each admissions office.
notes: You do not need Korean to be admitted to an English-taught programme, and you will need it to work part-time, to do an internship and to live well.
Most universities run free or heavily subsidised Korean classes for their own international students.

A university-wide English-medium percentage is an average across the whole institution. It is not a promise that your major runs in English for four years, and the question should be put to the department in writing.

feeContext.summary: Korea does not charge international students a different tuition rate from Korean students at most universities, so there is no EU/non-EU split to record. Tuition is charged per semester and varies sharply by faculty, with medicine and engineering highest and humanities lowest, and the private Seoul universities considerably above the national institutes.
feeContext.typicalRange: KAIST publishes 3,433,000 KRW per semester for its undergraduate programme, with national health insurance at 458,340 KRW and on-campus housing at 664,000 KRW per semester. It is the only official Korean figure quoted here and does not apply to any other university.
feeContext.priceYear: Not stated on the source page, read 2026-09-23

livingContext.housing: University dormitories are the standard and by far the easiest route for a first-year international student: cheap, on campus, and usually allocated with the admission. KAIST publishes 664,000 KRW (about €430 at the ECB rate of 24 September 2026) a semester for a place. The private Seoul market needs a large jeonse or wolse deposit that is impractical to raise from Denmark, so apply for the dormitory the moment an offer arrives.
livingContext.healthcare: International students staying more than six months are enrolled in the National Health Insurance Service and pay a monthly premium — KAIST puts it at 458,340 KRW (about €295 at the ECB rate of 24 September 2026) a semester. It is compulsory, and Korean healthcare is fast and inexpensive at the point of use. A Danish EHIC does not apply.
livingContext.workRights: Students on a D-2 visa may work part-time only with permission from the immigration office, and the hour limits have in recent years been tied to Korean language proficiency and academic standing. Confirm the current limits with the Korea Immigration Service before relying on part-time earnings.
livingContext.residency: EU citizenship gives no shortcut. The university issues a Certificate of Admission, you apply for a D-2 student visa at the Korean embassy in Copenhagen with proof of funds and criminal-record and tuberculosis checks, and you register for an Alien Registration Card within 90 days of arrival — without which there is no bank account and no phone contract.
funding: The KAIST Scholarship: tuition exempt for eight semesters, 350,000 KRW a month and medical insurance, decided from the admission application with no separate form, and held on a GPA above 2.7 out of 4.3 after the first year.

The Global Korea Scholarship, from the 2028 round for a May 2027 IB graduate (2027 needs a graduation certificate by 31 December 2026). In the 2027 round it covered tuition up to 5m KRW (about €3,200 at the ECB rate of 24 September 2026) a semester, a Korean language year, airfare and 14.4m KRW (about €9,300) a year during the degree, over five to seven years. Its Embassy Track invites 74 countries and Denmark is not one.

Most Korean universities award a standing tuition reduction to admitted international students, frequently renewable on grades. Ask each admissions office for the rate before comparing sticker prices; it changes the real number materially.

funding.note: A full degree outside the EU/EEA follows separate rules, with its own ties-to-Denmark form: check su.dk before budgeting.

sectorLandscape.summary: Korea's Ministry of Education divides higher education into more kinds than English-language guides usually show. Alongside the four-year 대학교 that every foreigner has heard of sit 전문대학 junior colleges, national 교육대학 for primary teachers, the special-law science and technology institutes, polytechnic colleges under the labour ministry rather than this one, and open and cyber universities. An IB Diploma opens the first three of those; the junior college is rarely mentioned to foreigners and is the nearest Korean relative of the Danish erhvervsakademi.

routes.what: The route everything else is described against. Four years to a bachelor's degree, six for medicine, Korean medicine, dentistry, pharmacy and veterinary medicine. Admission for an applicant schooled entirely abroad runs through a separate international track with its own rounds, its own documents and no Suneung. This is where every English-taught undergraduate programme named on this page sits.
routes.note: Divided again into national, public and private, and the difference is money: the private Seoul universities charge considerably more than the national ones and are where most of the English-medium provision is.

routes.what: Two or three years, practical, aimed at a named occupation, ending in a diploma or an associate degree rather than a bachelor's. Strong in nursing and allied health, hotel and culinary work, design, early-years teaching, automotive and mechatronics. Several run a 전공심화과정 top-up that converts the associate degree into a bachelor's.
routes.note: Rarely mentioned to foreign applicants. Whether the international track exists here in practice, and in what language, is not known; a student who needs it will not find it in the ordinary listings.

routes.what: KAIST, GIST, DGIST and UNIST: research institutes founded under their own statutes rather than the ordinary universities act, small, heavily funded, and the part of Korean higher education that teaches undergraduates in English as a matter of institutional policy. Undergraduates commonly enter without a declared major and choose after a common first year.
routes.note: They do not behave like the rest of the system. KAIST runs two international rounds. The Early round (closes 22 October 2026) starts at the end of February 2027; only the Regular round (closes 14 January 2027, results 25 March) leads to the September intake, more than seven months after it closes.

routes.what: Ten or so national institutions that exist to train primary school teachers, four years, tightly tied to the state teaching examination and to placement in Korean schools.
routes.note: Named because it is a visible part of the sector and because it is an example of a route that exists and is not open to this reader: teaching in Korean primary schools is not a path an international applicant enters through.

routes.what: Short, employment-focused technical training under the Ministry of Employment and Labour rather than the Ministry of Education. Welding, industrial automation, electrical work, machining — the trades side of post-secondary study.
routes.note: Missing from most education-ministry material because it belongs to a different ministry, which is exactly why it is worth naming. Not covered here beyond its existence.

routes.englishName: cyber university and the open university
routes.what: Distance and online degree provision, including the Korea National Open University. Full bachelor's degrees, taught in Korean, designed for people already working.
routes.note: Listed for completeness. Note that the Global Korea Scholarship explicitly excludes evening, short-term, online and distance programmes, so this route is outside any government funding a foreign student might reach.

notes: Audited 2026-09-24 (docs/research/audit/kr.md). Dates were read for Yonsei UIC, KAIST, Seoul National and Korea University; POSTECH and UNIST were checked for their international tracks. The other institutions are listed and their rounds unread.
Re-check in January 2027: Yonsei UIC's 2nd Round and Korea University's Fall 2027 round are both expected to be published in the spring of 2027, and neither has a day attached yet.

Not established: any published minimum IB point score at any Korean institution; how each university treats a conditional offer once results arrive on 6 July; the D-2 work-hour limits; and whether the international track reaches 전문대학 junior colleges at all.

Seoul National University's English admissions page links a Spring 2027 guideline written in Korean. Only its schedule table and the two admission-type headings were read; the eligibility text was not.
